threads.body: Regenerate `scenarios/http/js/package-lock.json` after this bump. Its embedded manifest for `@otel-conformance/scenario-sdk` still requests `@opentelemetry/sdk-node` 0.221.0, and the lockfile no longer contains any `node_modules/@opentelemetry/sdk-node` package. Because scenario setup runs `npm ci` from that lockfile, the shared SDK dependency is currently stale/missing and the scenarios cannot reliably load the newly declared 0.223.0 package.

replies.body: Fixed in 0b4a95e4. The regenerated workspace lockfile now snapshots `@opentelemetry/sdk-node` at `0.223.0` and includes its complete dependency graph. Relock now discards cached copied `file:` package snapshots before invoking npm, so it reads the current local manifests instead of retaining stale dependencies. HTTP JavaScript scenarios and all other checks pass on the current head, 4f9eff3b.

threads.body: If npm exits with an error or cannot start, `refresh_local_packages` has already removed the copied-package entries from the lockfile. Nothing restores them, so a previously complete lockfile is left missing required packages and subsequent `npm ci` runs can fail. Preserve the original bytes and restore them whenever regeneration does not succeed. Add regression coverage for both a nonzero exit and a subprocess exception.

+def refresh_local_packages(project: Path) -> None:
+    """Discard copied file-package snapshots so npm reads their manifests."""
+    path = project / BUILD_MARKER
+    lock = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    packages = lock.get("packages", {})
+    copied = [
+        name
+        for name, package in packages.items()
+        if package.get("resolved", "").startswith("file:")
+        and not package.get("link")
+    ]
+    if copied:
+        for name in copied:
+            del packages[name]
+        path.write_text(
+            json.dumps(lock, indent=2) + "\n",
+            encoding="utf-8",
+            newline="\n",
+        )
+

threads.body: These regenerated entries replace public npm tarball URLs with the relocking environment's Azure Artifacts mirror. `npm ci` follows the locked URLs, so installations now require access to that additional host even when the configured registry is `registry.npmjs.org`. Networks that allow only the public npm registry will fail to install this dependency graph. Regenerate the affected entries against `https://registry.npmjs.org/`, retaining public-registry integrity metadata rather than the SHA-1 values introduced for several unchanged packages.
